### 1. What's Life Like in This Ward?
In summer, our homes turn like ovens under the blazing sun, especially with 0 trees and parks to give us cool shade. When it rains, nearly every road faces pani bharaav because over 98% of our streets have no drains to carry water away. On top of that, 8 out of 10 slum homes have no proper underground sewer pipes, making daily life messy and hard.

---

### 2. Problems and What We Can Do About Them

| Problem | How Bad Is It? | Why Does This Happen Here? | What Can Be Done? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Street flooding | Terrible. Over 98% of roads have no working drains at all. | Rainwater has nowhere to escape, so water collects right on the streets. | Build roadside drains that carry rainwater away into the main naala. |
| Extreme heat | Very tough. Temperatures climb up to 34.3°C with no open green cover. | Hot concrete and metal tin sheets trap the heat inside our rooms. | Put white heat-reflecting paint for rooftops to keep rooms cool inside. |
| No trees or shade | Bad. There are 0 recorded trees or parks in our area. | Fast construction has covered every open patch of earth with cement. | Plant roadside shade trees like neem and peepal wherever space permits. |
| Dirty water overflow | Serious health risk. 80% of slum homes lack sewer pipe connections. | Dirty household waste flows into open street paths instead of closed pipes. | Lay basic underground sewer lines to connect every home safely. |

---

### 3. How Will the Money, Workers and Time Be Used?

| Work To Be Done | How Many? | Money (Rs.) | Workers Needed | Time Needed | Who Is Responsible? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| White heat-reflecting paint for rooftops | 6 building clusters | Rs. 720,000 | 12 | 1 month | PMC Building & Development Department |

**Summary:**
- **Total money being used:** Rs. 720,000 out of Rs. 1,300,000
- **Money left over:** Rs. 580,000
- **Workers needed:** 12 person-months
- **Everything done in:** 1 months

---

### 4. What Should the Ward Officer Do? (Step by Step)

1. **Week 1:** Visit the crowded residential areas in Ganesh Nagar, check the rooftops that get hottest, and talk to residents so they know the painting work is starting.
2. **Week 2:** Purchase good-quality white heat-reflecting roof paint and bring together the team of 12 workers with proper brushes, rollers, and safety gear.
3. **Week 3:** Clean all selected roofs thoroughly to remove dust and apply the first coat of white cooling paint across all 6 building clusters.
4. **Week 4:** Apply the final second coat, inspect the finished roofs with local residents, and plan how to use the remaining Rs. 580,000 to clear choked naalas.

---

### 5. How Will Residents Know Things Are Getting Better?

- ✅ Homes with white-painted roofs will feel noticeably cooler in the afternoon, so fans do not blow burning hot air.
- ✅ Families, especially small kids and elders, will be able to rest inside during peak afternoon heat without getting headaches.
- ✅ Electricity bills will stay lower because desert coolers and fans will not have to run at full speed all day long.
